title: I rent a room in Melaka for work. Subsale or new launch home?
excerpt: A single first-time buyer posted to Melaka wants to stop renting and is torn between a subsale and a new project. Sean asks why buy a home there at all, and suggests an investment unit first.

question.asker: From C, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: C works in Melaka but isn't from there, and rents a room. C is a first-time buyer, single, and wants a place of their own soon. Subsales seem to involve more paperwork, a slower loan and an older house, while the new project C likes won't be ready until June 2024.
question.text: Should a first-time buyer pick a subsale or a new project, and what are the pros and cons of each?

answer.quote: Build cash flow vehicles first before seeking for comfort.
answer.summary: First ask why C needs a home in Melaka now. Unless C's career or partner means settling there, Sean would rent on and buy an investment unit in KL whose rent covers the instalment. A home to live in can come later, when life is settled.

reasons.title: Renting fits a temporary posting
reasons.body: Rent pays for space you need for a few uncertain years. If C may be transferred, owning a home there loses flexibility, and buyers who move often end up paying for an empty house and a rental elsewhere.

reasons.title: Subsale and new launch differ in cash and time
reasons.body: A freehold subsale takes about three to six months to transfer, and leasehold three or four months more for state consent, which varies by state. It needs about 18% up front in cash, while a new launch is a one-stop deal with financing but is often priced higher for the wait.

reasons.title: An own-stay home rarely makes money
reasons.body: Over 35 years the interest roughly doubles what you pay, so a RM500,000 home sold for RM1 million later barely breaks even. What you get is certainty and a form of forced saving.

reasons.title: Let tenants build your equity
reasons.body: A unit renting at about 4.5% to 5% of its price can cover its own instalment, so tenants pay it off while the value grows. Sean found several KL projects that would roughly break even at current rents.

actions: Decide first whether you are settling in Melaka for career or family.
If not, keep renting there and look for an investment unit in KL with a 4.5% to 5% rental yield.
If buying a subsale, budget about 18% of the price in cash and allow extra months for a leasehold title.
If buying a new launch, check the handover date against how long you will keep renting.
Keep the bigger own-stay or landed home for when your family and career are settled.
caveat: If C has settled in Melaka to build a career or family, buying a home to live in there makes sense, and the subsale versus new launch choice then comes down to cash and timing.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #201. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as Sean stated them in February 2023. Transfer times and state consent rules differ by state and change over time.
